mainTopic: Training children to fast on יום הכפורים; feeding the pregnant and the sick; פיקוח נפש and the three sins of יהרג ואל יעבור
overview: The משנה says children are not made to fast on יום הכפורים, but they are trained one or two years before adulthood. רב חסדא explains that a weak child starts one year early and a healthy child two years early. רב הונא, רב נחמן and רבי יוחנן then give age charts for fasting a few hours, a full fast מדרבנן, and a full fast מדאורייתא. רבי יוחנן says there is no rabbinic full-fast stage at all. The גמרא tests each side against the משנה and a ברייתא, and every view survives. רבא בר עולא concludes that there are two kinds of training: delaying meals for young children, and a full fast for older ones. A new משנה rules that a pregnant woman with a craving, or a sick person, is fed on יום הכפורים. A ברייתא explains that פיקוח נפש overrides every איסור except עבודה זרה, גילוי עריות and שפיכות דמים. The גמרא then gives the source for each of those three exceptions.

steps.title: The משנה: children are trained to fast before adulthood
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that young children are not made to fast on יום הכפורים, but they are trained one or two years before adulthood so they get used to מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Children are not made to fast on יום הכפורים. But we train them one year before and two years before adulthood, so that they will be used to doing מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה states the basic rule. Little children don't fast, but shortly before they become adults we start training them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two parts here. First, there is no real obligation of עינוי for a child. Second, there is still a duty of חינוך: getting the child used to the מצוה before it becomes a real obligation. The משנה mentions two time frames, 'a year before' and 'two years before,' and the גמרא will ask about this next.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
The children, one does not afflict them (make them fast)
on Yom Kippur;
but one trains them
one year before and two years before (adulthood),
so that they will be accustomed to מצוות.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַתִּינוֹקוֹת אֵין מְעַנִּין אוֹתָן בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opening of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Children do not have to fast on יום הכפורים, but they are trained one or two years before adulthood so they get used to מצוות.

steps.title: Why does the משנה need to say 'one year before'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if we already train children two years early, then of course we train them one year early. Why mention both?
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Now, if we train them two years before, is it necessary to say that we train them one year before?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the משנה. 'One year before' looks unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If training starts two years before adulthood, it obviously continues during the last year. So writing 'one year before' seems to add nothing. The גמרא is asking what extra case 'one year' is meant to teach.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, i.e., 'since already'; introduces an 'obviously' argument

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Now, if two years before we train them,
is it necessary to say one year before?

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא בִּפְנֵי שְׁתַּיִם מְחַנְּכִין לְהוּ — בִּפְנֵי שָׁנָה מִבַּעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה's wording
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's phrase 'one year before and two years before'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The larger time frame (two years) already includes the smaller one (one year), so mentioning one year seems pointless.

steps.title: רב חסדא: a weak child versus a healthy child
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that the two numbers are for two different kinds of children. A weak child is trained one year before, and a healthy child two years before.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: It is not difficult. This (one year) is for a sick or weak child; that (two years) is for a healthy child.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question. Each time frame in the משנה is about a different type of child.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is not giving one long range. It is giving two separate starting points. A weak child only begins one year early. A healthy child begins two years early. So neither phrase is extra.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (standard answer formula)

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said: It is not difficult:
this (one year before) is for a weak child;
that (two years before) is for a healthy child.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא, לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא — בְּחוֹלֶה, הָא — בְּבָרִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about extra wording
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each phrase refers to a different type of child
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה gives one range, so 'one year' is unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each number is a separate starting age: one year for a weak child, two years for a healthy child.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's 'one year' and 'two years' are two separate cases: a חולה starts one year before adulthood, and a בריא starts two years before.

steps.title: רב הונא's age chart (for girls)
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא: at ages 8–9 a child fasts for a few hours; at 10–11 she finishes the fast מדרבנן; at 12 a girl finishes it מדאורייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: At eight and nine, we train the child to fast for some hours. At ten and eleven, they complete the fast by rabbinic law. At twelve, they complete the fast by Torah law. This is about a girl.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רב הונא's detailed timeline for how fasting builds up. This is for a girl, who becomes an adult at twelve.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא describes three stages. First, a partial fast for hours (לשעות). Next, a full fast required by the rabbis (משלימין מדרבנן). Last, a full fast required by the Torah once she reaches adulthood. The two years of rabbinic full fasting match the משנה's 'one year and two years before.'

keyTerms.meaning: For hours, i.e., a partial fast

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'לשעות' (fasting only some hours) with 'משלימין' (fasting the whole day). They are two different stages of training.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן שְׁמוֹנֶה וּבֶן תֵּשַׁע — מְחַנְּכִין אוֹתוֹ לְשָׁעוֹת.
phrases.english: At eight and nine years old, one trains him (to fast) for hours.
At ten and eleven years old,
they complete (the fast) by rabbinic law;
at twelve years old,
they complete (the fast) by Torah law. This is for a girl.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: בֶּן שְׁמוֹנֶה וּבֶן תֵּשַׁע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion that defines the age stages of training
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Girls: ages 8–9 fast for hours; 10–11 full fast מדרבנן; 12 full fast מדאורייתא.

steps.title: רב נחמן's age chart (for boys)
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן: at 9–10 a child fasts for hours; at 11–12 he finishes the fast מדרבנן; at 13 a boy finishes it מדאורייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן said: At nine and ten, we train them to fast for hours. At eleven and twelve, they complete the fast by rabbinic law. At thirteen, they complete the fast by Torah law. This is about a boy.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives the same three-stage plan, but each stage is one year later because it is for a boy, who becomes an adult at thirteen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The structure is the same as רב הונא's: hours, then a rabbinic full fast, then a Torah full fast. It is simply shifted up one year to match a boy's בר מצוה age. Both opinions keep a two-year stage of full rabbinic fasting before adulthood.

keyTerms.meaning: Thirteen years old (a boy's age of adulthood)

phrases.english: And Rav Nachman said:

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן תֵּשַׁע בֶּן עֶשֶׂר — מְחַנְּכִין אוֹתָן לְשָׁעוֹת,
phrases.english: At nine and ten years old, one trains them (to fast) for hours;

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן אַחַת עֶשְׂרֵה בֶּן שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה —
phrases.english: at eleven and twelve years old,
they complete (the fast) by rabbinic law;

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן שְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה — מַשְׁלִימִין מִדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא בְּתִינוֹק.
phrases.english: at thirteen years old, they complete it by Torah law. This is for a boy.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: בֶּן תֵּשַׁע בֶּן עֶשֶׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel opinion: the same structure, applied to boys
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Boys: ages 9–10 fast for hours; 11–12 full fast מדרבנן; 13 full fast מדאורייתא.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: no stage of a rabbinic full fast
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says there is no such thing as a rabbinic full fast for children. At 10–11 they fast for hours, and at 12 the full fast is already מדאורייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: There is no rabbinic requirement to complete the fast. At ten and eleven, we train them to fast for hours. At twelve, they complete the fast by Torah law.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן disagrees with the middle stage. In his view, a child only fasts for hours until adulthood, and then fasts fully because of Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא and רב נחמן have three stages. רבי יוחנן has only two: partial fasting, then a Torah-level full fast. This raises a question: how does רבי יוחנן explain the משנה's 'one year and two years before'? The גמרא will test this next.

keyTerms.meaning: There is not / does not exist

steps.whyThisMatters: This opinion removes the middle stage. That makes it harder to fit with the משנה, and it sets up the challenge that follows.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
There is no rabbinic (requirement of) completing the fast.

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן עֶשֶׂר בֶּן אַחַת עֶשְׂרֵה — מְחַנְּכִין אוֹתוֹ לְשָׁעוֹת,
phrases.english: At ten and eleven years old, one trains him (to fast) for hours;
at twelve years old, they complete (the fast) by Torah law.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: הַשְׁלָמָה דְּרַבָּנַן לֵיכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב הונא and רב נחמן about the middle stage
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no rabbinic full fast for children. Ages 10–11 fast for hours, and at 12 the full fast is מדאורייתא.

steps.title: Testing the opinions against the משנה: it fits רב הונא and רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה again and says it fits רב הונא and רב נחמן well. Both 'one year before' and 'two years before' refer to the full fast that is required 'by their words,' meaning מדרבנן. This sets up a challenge against רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: Children are not made to fast on יום הכפורים, but we train them one year before and two years before. This works well for רב הונא and רב נחמן: 'one year before' and 'two years before' both mean a full fast by rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It quotes the משנה again and shows that the משנה fits easily with רב הונא and רב נחמן. This prepares a question against רבי יוחנן, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב הונא and רב נחמן, 'one year before' (a weak child) and 'two years before' (a healthy child) both describe the rabbinic full-fast stage, called 'לדבריהן' (by the rabbis' words). רבי יוחנן says there is no rabbinic full fast at all. So the 'בשלמא' implies that for him the משנה is harder to explain.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, this works for... (sets up a contrast)
By their words, i.e., by rabbinic law

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה is quoted a second time here for a new reason. Before, it was a question about wording. Now it is being used as a test against the אמוראים' opinions.

phrases.english: We learned (in the Mishnah):

phrases.aramaic: הַתִּינוֹקוֹת אֵין מְעַנִּין אוֹתָן בַּיּוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים,
phrases.english: The children, one does not afflict them on Yom Kippur;
but one trains them
one year before and two years before.
Granted, according to Rav Huna and Rav Nachman,
(it makes sense to say) one year before and two years before:
one year before (a weak child), by their (rabbinic) words;
and two years before (a healthy child), by their (rabbinic) words.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: הַתִּינוֹקוֹת אֵין מְעַנִּין אוֹתָן בַּיּוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the משנה to test the three opinions; begins a challenge against רבי יוחנן
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's statement that there is no rabbinic full fast
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's 'one year and two years before' fits neatly as a rabbinic full fast (לדבריהן) for רב הונא and רב נחמן. That suggests רבי יוחנן, who denies a rabbinic full fast, will have trouble explaining it.

steps.title: The משנה seems difficult for רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the challenge it set up: the משנה fits רב הונא and רב נחמן, but it seems difficult for רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבי יוחנן, is it difficult?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes the challenge from Step 7. If the משנה is talking about a rabbinic full fast, how can רבי יוחנן say there is no such thing?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 7 the גמרא showed that 'one year or two years before' fits a rabbinic full fast. רבי יוחנן says there is no rabbinic full fast for children. So he seems to have no way to explain the משנה's two numbers.

keyTerms.meaning: But (here: but on the other hand)

phrases.english: But according to Rabbi Yochanan, is it difficult?
phrases.notes: This finishes the 'בשלמא' question that started back in Step 7.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge that Step 7 set up
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view that there is no rabbinic full fast for children
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's 'one or two years before' seems to describe a rabbinic full fast, and רבי יוחנן denies that such a fast exists.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן reads the years as right before maturity
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that 'one year or two' means the years right before the child becomes an adult.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן would tell you: What does 'one year or two' mean? The years close to their maturity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן. The 'one or two years' in the משנה are simply the years just before adulthood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן says the one or two years are the years right before the child reaches maturity. A weak child practices for one year, and a healthy child for two. During those years the child fasts for some hours, so the משנה does not need a separate rabbinic full fast.

keyTerms.meaning: He would say to you (a defense on someone's behalf)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan would say to you:
What is meant by 'one year or two'?
Close to their maturity.
phrases.notes: These are the years right before adulthood, not an extra rabbinic stage.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 8
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'One or two years before' means a rabbinic full-fast stage
steps.terutzMaskana: 'One or two years' are simply the years right before maturity, when a weak child practices one year and a healthy child two

steps.title: A ברייתא that fits רבי יוחנן challenges רב הונא and רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says children are not made to fast, only trained one or two years before maturity. This fits רבי יוחנן but is difficult for רב הונא and רב נחמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear what רבה בר שמואל taught: Children are not made to fast on יום הכפורים, but they are trained one or two years before their maturity. This fits רבי יוחנן, but it is difficult for רב הונא and רב נחמן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא. It sounds like children only get 'training,' never a rabbinic full fast, so now רב הונא and רב נחמן are under pressure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference from the משנה is the added words 'סמוך לפירקן', meaning right before maturity. The ברייתא calls those last one or two years 'training'. That matches רבי יוחנן, who has two years of partial fasting just before maturity. רב הונא and רב נחמן say those same years are already a full fast מדרבנן, with partial fasting coming earlier.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not afflict (do not make them fast)

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתָנֵי רַבָּה בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Come and hear, for Rabba bar Shmuel taught:
Children, we do not make them fast
on Yom Kippur,
but we train them
one year or two years close to their maturity.
Granted, according to Rabbi Yochanan it works out well,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְרַב הוּנָא וּלְרַב נַחְמָן — קַשְׁיָא!
phrases.english: but according to Rav Huna and Rav Nachman it is difficult!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתָנֵי רַבָּה בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רבי יוחנן, the גמרא turns the challenge onto רב הונא and רב נחמן
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא and רב נחמן's view that there are years of a rabbinic full fast
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא calls the one or two years right before maturity (סמוך לפירקן) years of 'training'. For רב הונא and רב נחמן, those years are a full fast מדרבנן, not training.

steps.title: Training in the ברייתא means a full fast
steps.stepSummary: The answer for רב הונא and רב נחמן: the 'training' in the ברייתא means a full fast.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis would tell you: What is the 'training' that it teaches? Completing the fast.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב הונא and רב נחמן. It says the word 'training' in this ברייתא means a complete fast.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'training' means a full fast, then the ברייתא is describing the rabbinic full-fast years. That is exactly what רב הונא and רב נחמן hold. 'We do not afflict them' would then refer to younger children.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis would say to you

phrases.english: The Rabbis would say to you:
phrases.notes: Here 'רבנן' means רב הונא and רב נחמן.

phrases.english: What is the 'training' that it also teaches?
Completion of the fast.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי לָךְ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining a key word in the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Training' means only partial fasting, so there is no rabbinic full fast
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Training' here means a full fast, which is the rabbinic full-fast stage

steps.title: Another ברייתא shows training means delaying meals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether 'training' can mean a full fast. Another ברייתא defines training as pushing the meal back by an hour.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is training ever called completion? But a ברייתא teaches: What is training? If he usually ate at the second hour, we feed him at the third. If he usually ate at the third, we feed him at the fourth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of Step 11. A different ברייתא clearly uses 'training' to mean delaying a meal by an hour, not fasting all day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in Step 11 depended on 'training' meaning a full fast. This ברייתא defines training as small steps, such as eating an hour later than usual. So 'training' seems to mean partial fasting, and the defense of רב הונא and רב נחמן is weakened.

keyTerms.meaning: And is it called...? (a challenging question)
But it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: And is training called completion?
But it was taught in a Baraita:
What is training?
If he was used to eating at the second hour,
we feed him at the third.
If at the third, we feed him at the fourth.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי קָרֵי לְחִינּוּךְ הַשְׁלָמָה, וְהָא תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the definition given in Step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'training' means a full fast
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא explicitly defines training as delaying a meal by an hour, which is partial fasting.

steps.title: There are two kinds of training
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר עולא answers that there are two kinds of training: delaying meals for younger children, and full fasting for older ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר עולא said: There are two kinds of training.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the conflict. Both ברייתות are right because 'training' can mean two different things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For younger children, training means delaying meals by an hour or so. For older children close to maturity, training means a full fast. So the ברייתא of רבה בר שמואל can mean a full fast, and רב הונא and רב נחמן are defended.
steps.whatToRemember: Every view survives. רבי יוחנן reads 'one or two years' as the years right before maturity. רב הונא and רב נחמן read 'training' as a full fast. 'Training' has two levels: delaying meals for young children, and a full fast for older children.

phrases.english: Rava bar Ulla said:
There are two kinds of training.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא בַּר עוּלָּא: תְּרֵי חִנּוּכֵי הָווּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing two meanings of one term
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Training' has only one meaning, delaying meals
steps.terutzMaskana: There are two trainings: delaying meals for young children, and a full fast for older children

steps.title: New משנה: feeding a pregnant woman who smelled food
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: a pregnant woman who smelled food and craves it is fed on יום הכפורים until she recovers.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A pregnant woman who smelled food is fed until she recovers.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It rules that a pregnant woman with a strong craving from smelling food may eat on יום הכפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A strong craving in pregnancy may endanger her or the baby. So we feed her, but only until she feels settled. Once she is calm again, she does not need more.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (start of a new משנה)
Until she recovers / her spirit is settled

steps.whyThisMatters: This opens the topic of when danger to life allows eating on יום הכפורים.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
A pregnant woman who smelled food,
we feed her until she recovers.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ עוּבָּרָה שֶׁהֵרִיחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A pregnant woman who smelled food is fed until she recovers

steps.title: Feeding a sick person based on experts or his own word
steps.stepSummary: A sick person is fed based on the experts. If there are no experts, he is fed based on his own word until he says 'enough'.
steps.simpleTranslation: A sick person is fed based on experts. If there are no experts there, he is fed based on his own word until he says 'enough'.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a second case. It tells us whose opinion decides whether a sick person eats on יום הכפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First we follow the experts who know medicine. If none are there, we trust the sick person himself. We keep feeding him until he says he has had enough.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as meaning the sick person's word counts only when no expert is around for any purpose. The משנה only sets an order for when experts are absent. The גמרא will later discuss what happens when the experts and the patient disagree.

phrases.english: A sick person, we feed him
according to experts,
and if there are no experts there,
we feed him according to himself
until he says 'enough'.

steps.triggerLanguage: חוֹלֶה — מַאֲכִילִין אוֹתוֹ עַל פִּי בְּקִיאִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second case in the same משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sick person is fed based on experts. Without experts, he is fed based on his own word until he says 'enough'.

steps.title: A pregnant woman who craves forbidden meat is fed step by step
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches how to feed a pregnant woman who craves קדשים or pig meat. First give her a reed dipped in the gravy. If that does not help, give her the gravy itself. If that does not help, give her the fat itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא: The Rabbis taught: If a pregnant woman smelled holy meat or pig meat and craves it, we dip a thin reed into its gravy and put it on her mouth. If she calms down, good. If not, we feed her the gravy itself. If she calms down, good. If not, we feed her the fat itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts explaining the משנה about the pregnant woman by quoting a ברייתא. The ברייתא lays out exactly how she should be fed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only said 'feed her until she recovers.' The ברייתא adds the method: start with the smallest amount of the forbidden food and go up only if needed. Even when a life is in danger, we try to break the איסור as little as possible.

keyTerms.meaning: Consecrated (sacrificial) meat, forbidden to her here
Gravy or juice of the meat
Her mind became settled (the craving calmed)
Fat (here, the substance of the meat itself)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical rule for every case of פיקוח נפש: do what is needed, but start with the least severe step.

phrases.english: Gemara: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: עוּבָּרָה שֶׁהֵרִיחָה בְּשַׂר קוֹדֶשׁ אוֹ בְּשַׂר חֲזִיר —
phrases.english: A pregnant woman who smelled holy meat or pig meat —
phrases.notes: She craves it, and her life (or the baby's) may be in danger.

phrases.english: we stick a reed into the gravy for her,
and place it on her mouth,
if she calms down — good,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לָאו — מַאֲכִילִין אוֹתָהּ רוֹטֶב עַצְמוֹ,
phrases.english: and if not — we feed her the gravy itself,
and if she calms down — good,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לָאו — מַאֲכִילִין אוֹתָהּ שׁוּמָּן עַצְמוֹ.
phrases.english: and if not — we feed her the fat itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: עוּבָּרָה שֶׁהֵרִיחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה from step 14 by spelling out how the pregnant woman is fed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Feed her in stages: a reed dipped in gravy, then the gravy, then the fat. Stop as soon as she is calm.

steps.title: Nothing stands in the way of saving a life except three sins
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives the reason: פיקוח נפש overrides every איסור except עבודה זרה, גילוי עריות and שפיכות דמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because there is nothing that stands in the way of פיקוח נפש, except עבודה זרה, גילוי עריות, and שפיכות דמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains why we may feed her forbidden food. It states a big general rule about saving lives, with three exceptions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pig meat case is one example of a wider principle: almost every איסור is pushed aside to save a life. The three exceptions are sins a person must die rather than commit. The rest of the sugya looks for the source of each exception.
steps.whatToRemember: פיקוח נפש overrides everything except three sins: עבודה זרה, גילוי עריות and שפיכות דמים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic source for the three sins of יהרג ואל יעבור (be killed rather than transgress).

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין לְךָ דָּבָר שֶׁעוֹמֵד בִּפְנֵי פִּקּוּחַ נֶפֶשׁ,
phrases.english: For there is nothing that stands in the way of saving a life,
except for idol worship
and forbidden relations and murder.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁאֵין לְךָ דָּבָר שֶׁעוֹמֵד בִּפְנֵי פִּקּוּחַ נֶפֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind the feeding procedure in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פיקוח נפש overrides all איסורים except עבודה זרה, גילוי עריות and שפיכות דמים.

steps.title: Where do we learn that עבודה זרה is an exception?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that one must give up his life rather than worship idols.
steps.simpleTranslation: עבודה זרה — from where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: This step sets up the next move. The גמרא asks for the source of the first exception, עבודה זרה, and the answer comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the Torah lets us break a מצוה to save a life. So an exception needs a clear source. The גמרא wants to know where the Torah says that עבודה זרה is different.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know it?

phrases.english: Idol worship — from where do we know?

steps.triggerLanguage: עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the first exception listed in step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source that one must die rather than commit עבודה זרה.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר asks why the verse says both 'soul' and 'might'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. רבי אליעזר notes that the verse in קריאת שמע says both 'בכל נפשך' and 'בכל מאדך', and asks why both are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי אליעזר says: If it says 'with all your soul,' why does it say 'with all your might'? And if it says 'with all your might,' why does it say 'with all your soul'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts answering by quoting רבי אליעזר. He first points out that the verse seems to repeat itself, which sets up his explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you must love ה׳ even with your life (נפש), then giving up your money (מאד) seems obvious. If the Torah needed to say money, then saying life seems unnecessary. Each phrase looks extra, so each must teach something.

keyTerms.meaning: With all your soul (even your life)
With all your might (understood here as your money)
Why was it stated? (a phrase seems extra)

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
If it is said 'with all your soul,'
why is it said 'with all your might'?
And if it is said 'with all your might,'
why is it said 'with all your soul'?

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: אִם נֶאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering step 18 by bringing רבי אליעזר's question on the verse.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is the verse 'ואהבת את ה' אלקיך... בכל נפשך ובכל מאדך'. Its seemingly extra wording is explained in the next step.

steps.title: Each person is told to give up what he values most
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר explains: some people value their body more, so the Torah says 'with all your soul'. Others value their money more, so the Torah says 'with all your might'. Loving ה׳, which means not serving idols, requires giving up even one's life.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there is a person whose body is dearer to him than his money, for him it says 'with all your soul.' And if there is a person whose money is dearer to him than his body, for him it says 'and with all your might.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר answers his own question. Each phrase speaks to a different type of person, and this proves that one must die rather than serve idols.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each phrase is needed, because people value different things. 'בכל נפשך' teaches that you must give up even your life for your love of ה׳, and not turn to עבודה זרה. This is the source that עבודה זרה is not overridden by פיקוח נפש.
steps.confusionAlert: The verse does not say 'עבודה זרה'. The link is that 'loving ה׳ with all your soul' means staying loyal to Him even at the cost of your life, and serving idols is the opposite of that loyalty.
steps.whatToRemember: The source for dying rather than serving idols is 'בכל נפשך', which means even if He takes your life.

phrases.english: If you have a person
whose body is dearer to him than his money —
that is why it says 'with all your soul,'
and if you have a person
whose money is dearer to him than his body —
that is why it says 'and with all your might.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם יֵשׁ לְךָ אָדָם שֶׁגּוּפוֹ חָבִיב עָלָיו מִמָּמוֹנוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves רבי אליעזר's question from step 19 and completes the source for עבודה זרה.
steps.raayaObject: That one must give up his life rather than commit עבודה זרה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The verse 'בכל נפשך ובכל מאדך' as explained by רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: Where do we learn the exceptions of גילוי עריות and שפיכות דמים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now asks for the source that one must die rather than commit גילוי עריות or שפיכות דמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: גילוי עריות and שפיכות דמים — from where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: This step sets up the next move. The גמרא moves to the other two exceptions and asks for their source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עבודה זרה now has its source. The remaining two exceptions from the ברייתא still need one, and the גמרא handles both of them together.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know it? (same as מנלן)

phrases.aramaic: גִּילּוּי עֲרָיוֹת וּשְׁפִיכַת דָּמִים מְנָא לַן —
phrases.english: Forbidden relations and murder — from where do we know?

steps.triggerLanguage: גִּילּוּי עֲרָיוֹת וּשְׁפִיכַת דָּמִים מְנָא לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the list in step 17 and asks about the other two exceptions.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source that one must die rather than commit גילוי עריות or שפיכות דמים.

steps.title: רבי quotes the verse comparing the betrothed girl to a murder victim
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא in which רבי quotes the verse about a נערה המאורסה who is attacked: 'just like a man who rises against his fellow and kills him, so is this matter.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי says: 'For just as a man rises against his fellow and murders him, so is this matter.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer by quoting רבי, who points to a verse that compares an attack on a betrothed girl to murder.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse is about a נערה המאורסה who was forced, so she is not punished. It describes her case using the picture of a murder. That comparison will be the key to the source for both exceptions.

keyTerms.meaning: So is this matter (the case of the betrothed girl)

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi says:
'For just as a man rises against his fellow
and murders him,
so is this matter.'
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק in דברים כב:כו, about a betrothed girl attacked in the field.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: כִּי כַּאֲשֶׁר יָקוּם אִישׁ עַל רֵעֵהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering step 21 by bringing רבי's verse.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is the verse that compares the betrothed girl's attacker to a murderer. How this works is explained afterward.

steps.title: What does a murderer teach us about the betrothed girl?
steps.stepSummary: רבי asks what point is being learned by comparing the betrothed girl's case to a murderer.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what idea did we learn from a murderer for a betrothed girl?
steps.whatsHappening: This step sets up the next move. רבי asks why the Torah compares these two cases, and the answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The law of the betrothed girl already seems clear: she was forced, so she is not guilty. So the comparison to murder must be teaching something new, maybe in both directions. The answer will produce the source for both גילוי עריות and שפיכות דמים.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not an objection that rejects the verse. It is רבי's own setup question, asking what the comparison is meant to teach.

phrases.english: And what idea did we learn
from a murderer for a betrothed girl?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מָה עִנְיָן לָמַדְנוּ מֵרוֹצֵחַ לְנַעֲרָה הַמְאוֹרָסָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the purpose of the comparison in the verse from step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new law is learned from comparing the betrothed girl's case to murder.

steps.title: The comparison teaches in both directions: from the betrothed girl to the murderer
steps.stepSummary: The murderer case, which seemed only to teach about the נערה המאורסה, actually learns from her too. Just as one may save her by killing her attacker, so too one may save a murder victim by killing the murderer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this case came to teach and ends up being taught. Just as with a נערה המאורסה one is allowed to save her at the cost of the attacker's life, so too with a murderer, one may save the victim at the cost of the murderer's life.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבי's question from step 23. The verse's comparison does not only teach about the נערה. The murderer also learns a rule from her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a comparison uses a known case to teach about a new case. Here the murderer, the 'teacher', also becomes the 'student'. It is already known from elsewhere that one may save a נערה המאורסה by killing her attacker. Through the comparison, that same permission now applies to someone chasing another person to kill him.

keyTerms.term: הֲרֵי זֶה בָּא לְלַמֵּד וְנִמְצָא לָמֵד
keyTerms.meaning: This came to teach and ends up being taught. The comparison works in both directions.
A betrothed young woman. In the verse, she is attacked in the field.
One is allowed to save her at the cost of his (the attacker's) life
A murderer. Here it means one who is chasing someone to kill him.

steps.confusionAlert: The word 'בנפשו' (with his life) means the attacker's life, not the rescuer's. The rescuer may kill the attacker to stop the crime. He is not being told to risk his own life.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the halacha of a רודף. You may stop a would-be murderer, even by killing him, in order to save the victim.

phrases.english: Rather, this came to teach,
phrases.notes: The murderer case seemed to be only the 'teacher' in the comparison.

phrases.english: and it turns out to be taught:
phrases.notes: It also learns a rule from the נערה.

phrases.english: Just as a betrothed young woman
may be saved at the cost of his (the attacker's) life —
so too a murderer (etc.)
phrases.notes: The '(etc.)' stands for the rest of the line: so too the victim of a murderer may be saved by killing the murderer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: הֲרֵי זֶה בָּא לְלַמֵּד, וְנִמְצָא לָמֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי's question in step 23 about what is learned from the murderer comparison.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the comparison of the נערה המאורסה to a murderer teach?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The comparison goes both ways. First, the murderer learns from the נערה that one may kill the attacker to save the victim.

steps.title: From the murderer to the betrothed girl: one must die rather than sin
steps.stepSummary: Just as with murder one must be killed rather than kill, so too with a נערה המאורסה one must be killed rather than sin with her. This gives the source for יהרג ואל יעבור in גילוי עריות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as with a murderer the rule is 'let him be killed and not transgress,' so too with a נערה המאורסה the rule is 'let him be killed and not transgress.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the two-way comparison. This time the rule flows from murder to the נערה, and this answers the question from step 21.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is already known that a person must give up his life rather than kill someone else. The comparison carries that rule over to the נערה המאורסה. Since she is one example of גילוי עריות, the rule of יהרג ואל יעבור covers all forbidden relations.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him be killed and not transgress. One must give up his life rather than commit this sin.

steps.whatToRemember: From one verse we get two rules. (1) You may kill a רודף to save his victim. (2) You must die rather than commit גילוי עריות, just as you must die rather than commit שפיכות דמים.
steps.confusionAlert: This step assumes we already know that a person must die rather than murder. The source for that rule about murder itself is not given here.
steps.whyThisMatters: Together with עבודה זרה (steps 19–20), this completes the three sins for which one must give up his life rather than transgress.

phrases.english: Just as with a murderer: let him be killed and not transgress —
so too with a betrothed young woman:
let him be killed and not transgress.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה רוֹצֵחַ יֵהָרֵג וְאַל יַעֲבוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the second direction of the two-way comparison begun in step 24.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The rule of יהרג ואל יעבור applies to גילוי עריות. It is learned from murder through the comparison with the נערה המאורסה.
